Three things come up more than anything else, and none of them are what you would expect.": three separate piles of letters stand in a row on the worn wooden desk, and her hands are laying the last handful onto the third pile, caught mid-placing.
A close shot from desk height, three-quarter from the front right: the three piles run away from us in a diagonal row, the grey post trays full of letters soft behind them.
Image 1 is her workroom: the same worn wooden desk, brick wall and sash window, copied exactly.
In frame: a woman's hands, fifty-seven, long knuckly fingers, short plain nails, rust-orange needlecord cuffs; exactly three piles of white A4 typed letters of different lengths, some stapled, with long window envelopes, untidy; her right hand holds the last handful just touching the third pile, her left hand rests flat on the desk beside the first pile. The piles fill the lower half of the frame. Nothing else on the desk.
Soft morning daylight from the sash window, one direction. An ordinary iPhone photo.
No fourth pile, no readable text or logos, no handwriting, no face, no extra fingers.
